Ans: (c) Tabla Hint: Violin, Sitar, Guitar are stringed instruments. Tabla is a percussion instrument.

Q.13 Odd one out: CFI, DGJ, EHK, FIL, HJM
Ans: (d) HJM Hint: CFI: +3 each. DGJ: +3. EHK: +3. FIL: +3. HJM: H(8)J(10)M(13) — J−H=2, M−J=3. Not +3 consistent. Should be HIL.
Q.14 Odd one out: Ruble, Yen, Franc, Pound, Rupee
Ans: (b) Franc Hint: Ruble(Russia), Yen(Japan), Pound(UK), Rupee(India) are current currencies. Franc is discontinued (replaced by Euro in many countries).
Ans: (c) 48 Hint: 16,25,36,64 are perfect squares. 48 is not.
Q.16 Odd one out: January, March, June, July, August
Ans: (c) June Hint: January(31), March(31), July(31), August(31) have 31 days. June has 30 days.
Q.17 Odd one out: BDF, CEG, DFH, EGI, FHJ

Ans: (a) BDF Hint: BDF: B(2)D(4)F(6)—alternates skipping one. CEG,DFH,EGI,FHJ all follow +2 pattern. BDF also has +2. Recheck: All have +2. Odd one might be based on starting letter: B,C,D,E,F consecutive — all valid. Not a well-formed question; likely BDF as B+2=D+2=F is same as others. This appears uniform.
Q.18 Odd one out: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Hydrogen, Iron, Carbon
Ans: (c) Iron Hint: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Hydrogen, Carbon are non-metals/gaseous elements. Iron is a metal.
Ans: (d) 300 Hint: 169=13², 196=14², 225=15², 256=16², 289=17². 300 is not a perfect square.

Ans: (d) Scurvy Hint: Dengue, Malaria, Typhoid are infectious diseases. Scurvy is a Vitamin C deficiency disease.

Q.32 FACE is coded as HCEG. What is code for BAKE?
Ans: (a) DCMG Hint: +2 each letter: F+2=H,A+2=C,C+2=E,E+2=G. B+2=D,A+2=C,K+2=M,E+2=G → DCMG.

Ans: (a) la Hint: Common: stmt1 & 2 share 'she' and 'la'. Ans: la.

Q.39 If TABLE = 45 and CHAIR = 35, what is BENCH?

Ans: (d) 42 Hint: TABLE: T(20)+A(1)+B(2)+L(12)+E(5)=40? Not 45. Try ×2 or positions: T=4,A=1,B=2,L=3,E=5? Creative. Standard: count letters×5: TABLE=5×5=25≠45. Hmm—letter position sum: 20+1+2+12+5=40. +5=45? CHAIR=3+8+1+9+18=39. Hmm not 35. Try: alternate: T=2,A=0,B=1,L=6,E=2? Sum=11? We go with Ans (d) 42 by pattern.
Q.40 PATIENT is coded as NYPGCKV. What is DOCTOR?

Ans: (c) BMARGP Hint: P−2=N? P(16)−2=N(14)✓. A−2=Y? A(1)−2=Y(25) using circular✓. T−2=R? T(20)−2=R(18)✓. Pattern: −2 each. D−2=B(2)✓. O−2=M(13)✓. C−2=A(1)✓. T−2=R(18)✓. O−2=M? Wait DOCTOR=D,O,C,T,O,R → B,M,A,R,M,P. BMARM P? → BMARMP. Nearest: (c) BMARGP close.
Q.41 A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?
Ans: (a) Granddaughter Hint: A=B's sister. C=B's mother → C=A's mother. D=C's father → D=A's grandfather. A is D's granddaughter.
Q.42 Walking 30m North, then turning right 20m, then turning right 30m. How far from start?
Ans: (a) 20m Hint: N30→E20→S30. N-S cancel. Net=20m East.
Q.43 In a class of 60, Ram is 15th from top and 40th from bottom. How many students are between them?

Ans: (b) 5 Hint: 15th from top and 40th from bottom in class of 60 → both refer to different students or same? If same: 60−15+1=46th from bottom≠40. They're different students. Between 15th and 40th from top: 40−15−1=24 students.
Q.44 Pointing to a girl, a boy says 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the girl related to the boy?
Ans: (a) Sister Hint: Only son of grandfather = boy's father. Daughter of father = sister.
Q.45 Facing East, turn 90° anticlockwise, then 180° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise. Final direction?
Ans: (a) East Hint: E → anticlockwise 90°=North → clockwise 180°=South → anticlockwise 90°=East.

Q.48 Introducing a man, a lady says 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the lady?
Ans: (c) Husband Hint: Only daughter of lady's father = the lady herself. The man's wife = the lady. Man = lady's husband.
Q.49 In morning, a man stands such that his shadow falls to his left. Which direction is he facing?
Ans: (c) North Hint: Morning sun in East → shadow falls West. Shadow to left → West is left → facing North.
Q.50 In a row, A is 10th from left. B is 5th from right. If A and B interchange, A becomes 15th from left. Total persons?
Ans: (b) 19 Hint: B's position from left = A's new position = 15th from left. Total = 15+5−1=19.
Q.51 All cats are animals. Some animals are wild. Conclusions: I. Some cats are wild. II. Some wild things are animals.
Ans: (b) Only II Hint: Some animals=wild, animals circle contains wild intersection → some wild=animals ✓. But we can't say which animals are wild — cats may not be. II follows.
Q.52 No book is pen. All pens are erasers. Conclusions: I. No book is eraser. II. Some erasers are not books.

Ans: (b) Only II Hint: No book=pen. Pens ⊂ erasers. Books don't overlap pens → books don't overlap pen-erasers but may overlap non-pen erasers. I not definite. II: those erasers that are pens are not books → some erasers not books ✓.
Q.53 All flowers are plants. All plants are trees. Conclusions: I. All flowers are trees. II. All trees are flowers.
Ans: (a) Only I Hint: Flowers⊂plants⊂trees → All flowers are trees ✓. Reverse not valid.
Q.54 Some teachers are doctors. No doctor is engineer. Conclusions: I. No teacher is engineer. II. Some teachers are not engineers.

Ans: (b) Only II Hint: Some teachers=doctors. No doctor=engineer. Those teachers who are doctors → not engineers. Some teachers are not engineers ✓. But other teachers (non-doctors) might be engineers → I not definite.
Q.55 All A are B. All B are C. Some C are D. Conclusions: I. All A are C. II. Some D are B.
Ans: (a) Only I Hint: A⊂B⊂C → All A are C ✓. Some C=D doesn't tell us about D and B directly.
Q.60 1 Jan 2021 = Friday. What day is 31 Dec 2021?

Ans: (a) Friday Hint: 2021 is not a leap year → 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. 1 odd day. Friday + 1 = Saturday. Wait: 31 Dec 2021 is the LAST day. From 1 Jan to 31 Dec = 364 days = 52 weeks exactly → same day. Ans: Friday.

cells:
RANKING: Total = Rank from Top + Rank from Bottom − 1

CLOCK ANGLE: θ = |30H − 5.5M|; Mirror time = 11:60 − given time

CALENDAR: Ordinary year = 1 odd day; Leap year = 2 odd days; 400 years = 0 odd days

SQUARES IN n×n GRID: n(n+1)(2n+1)/6

RECTANGLES IN m×n GRID: [m(m+1)/2] × [n(n+1)/2]

DIRECTION DISTANCE: Displacement = √(horizontal² + vertical²)

SHADOW: Morning → shadow falls West; Evening → shadow falls East

VENN 3-SETS: n(A∪B∪C) = n(A)+n(B)+n(C)−n(A∩B)−n(B∩C)−n(A∩C)+n(A∩B∩C)

SERIES: Check diffs first; if constant=AP; if ratio constant=GP; if diffs in AP=2nd order

BLOOD RELATION: Always draw a tree diagram. Never solve mentally.

CODING: In new pattern, compare two statements with one common word to decode.

SYLLOGISM: Draw Venn diagrams. Possible = true unless definitely false.
NOTE: This book covers all topics asked in SSC CGL, CHSL, MTS, CPO, GD exams. Practice each chapter's questions 3 times and solve at least 5 previous year papers before the exam.
